title: Quasi-coherent modules are acyclic for big-fppf to small-etale direct image
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $W$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $M$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_W$-module on its small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Use the enlarged etale ringed model [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Choose a standard small big site $\mathcal B_W$ of algebraic spaces over $W$ in the size convention [def-weil-size-convention], with coverings the jointly surjective families of flat locally finitely presented morphisms, tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and structure sheaf $\mathcal O(V)=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$. Let $M^a$ be the fppf module sheaf whose sections at $v:V\to W$ are $\Gamma(V,v^*M)$, with tensor-pullback restriction [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The inclusion of etale $W$-objects into $\mathcal B_W$ induces a morphism of ringed topoi $a_W:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal B_W),\mathcal O)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(W_{\mathrm{et}}),\mathcal O_W)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], whose module direct image is restriction to those objects. Then $R^i a_{W,*}(M^a)=0$ for every $i>0$, where higher direct images are computed by injective module resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. No quasi-compactness, separation or finiteness hypothesis on $W$ or $M$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0DGN, lemma-review-quasi-coherent (7), for the morphism a_W described in section-fppf-etale-modules.

proof.text: All sites here are small in the chosen universe. Their module categories are Grothendieck abelian and hence have enough injectives. Apply the ringed-site cohomology-presheaf theorem to $a_W$ and $M^a$. For $q>0$, it identifies $R^qa_{W,*}M^a$ with $P^\#$, where $P(V)=R^q\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod},V}(M^a)$ for an etale $W$-object $V$. The derived-evaluation/slice comparison identifies this group with $H^q(\mathcal B_W/V,(M^a)_{ab}|_V)$. We will show $P(U)=0$ whenever $U\to W$ is an affine scheme etale chart.

Fix such a chart $u:U\to W$. The slice $\mathcal B_W/U$ is the big fppf site of spaces over $U$: send $(V\to W,V\to U)$ to $V\to U$, with inverse composition by $u$. Consider its full subcategory $(\mathit{Sch}/U)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. Every space over $U$ admits an etale scheme atlas, which is fppf. Scheme fppf coverings are precisely the space fppf coverings with scheme sources and target. The induced topology is therefore the scheme fppf topology: refine any space covering of a scheme by scheme atlases and compose, obtaining a scheme fppf covering; the converse uses the same covering comparison. Apply the dense-subsite equivalence with values in abelian groups to obtain restriction $E:\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal B_W/U)\simeq\operatorname{Ab}((\mathit{Sch}/U)_{\mathrm{fppf}})$. All atlases and refinements are taken in the fixed size convention.

source.place: Tag 0DFV, lemma-compare-cohomology-other-topologies, fppf case; 0DGN proof, final paragraph; spaces-topologies.tex 03Y8, 03Y9.

proof.text: The additive equivalence $E$ preserves kernels and cokernels by their universal properties, so it is exact. It preserves injectives: transport a monomorphism and a map to $E(I)$ through its inverse, extend the resulting map to $I$, and transport the extension back. It preserves terminal sections, since the terminal object on both sites is the same scheme $U$. Consequently, restricting an abelian injective resolution of $(M^a)_{ab}|_U$ gives an injective resolution on the scheme site with the identical complex of sections at $U$. Their cohomology groups agree.

source.place: Tag 0DFV, transport across the equivalence in the proof of 0DGN(7); resolution argument written out.

proof.text: The small-etale module $u^*M$ is quasi-coherent. The scheme Zariski/etale equivalence therefore gives a quasi-coherent Zariski module $F$ on $U$ and its canonical etale comparison $F_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq u^*M$. For any scheme $v:T\to U$, functoriality of that equivalence and the tensor composition comparison identify $(uv)^*M\simeq v^*(u^*M)\simeq(v^*F)_{\mathrm{et}}$. Thus the restriction of $M^a$ to the scheme fppf site has sections $\Gamma(T,v^*F)$, with the same restrictions: both send a section along $h:T'\to T$ to its tensor pullback and then use the canonical composition map. It is exactly $F^a$. The affine-scheme fppf acyclicity lemma gives $H^q((\mathit{Sch}/U)_{\mathrm{fppf}},(F^a)_{ab})=0$. Together with steps 1 and 3 this proves $P(U)=0$. No assertion about preservation of injectives by the forgetful module-to-abelian functor has been used.

source.place: Tag 0DEW, lemma-review-quasi-coherent, affine-cover argument for (7); spaces-more-cohomology.tex 0DGN, scheme comparison.

proof.text: Every etale space object $V\to W$ has an etale scheme atlas; refine its source by affine opens. This is an etale covering of $V$ by affine scheme objects over $W$, so $P$ vanishes on a covering of every object. If $N$ is any sheaf of modules and $b:P\to N$ a presheaf map, $b_V(s)$ restricts to zero on that covering for every $s\in P(V)$, hence is zero by separatedness of $N$. Thus every map $P\to N$ is the zero map. The sheafification adjunction now says $P^\#$ is initial in module sheaves, hence the zero module sheaf. Step 1 yields $R^qa_{W,*}M^a=0$ for every $q>0$. This includes $W=\varnothing$: its empty covering forces every module sheaf to be zero. No finite atlas, quasi-compactness or separatedness of $W$ was required.
